bannerLead: Helping youth thrive with independent-living skills — before, during, and beyond their stay.

stages.b: Youth build trust with staff before placement — creating connections that lay the foundation for a successful transition.
Life skills, mentorship, education, and career readiness inside a warm, structured home.
Expanded care: medical & dental, counseling, psychiatric care, and arts & hobby programs.

focusAreas.title: Money Management & Financial Literacy
focusAreas.body: Budgeting, smart spending, banking basics, credit confidence.

focusAreas.title: Housing & Daily Living
focusAreas.body: Routines, hygiene, meal prep, laundry, apartment readiness & maintenance.

focusAreas.title: Health & Wellness
focusAreas.body: Nutrition, exercise, sleep, mental-health check-ins, stress management.

focusAreas.title: Social-Emotional & Communication
focusAreas.body: Assertive communication, conflict resolution, online safety, healthy habits.

focusAreas.title: Employment & Education Skills
focusAreas.body: Resume writing, interview prep, workplace etiquette, time management, goal planning.

educationBody1: Youth attend public schools (Portland Public, Cleveland, Alliance), colleges & universities (Reed, PSU, Clackamas CC, Concordia), and trade & vocational programs (PCC Swan Island, NW College of Construction, NECA-IBEW, The Tech Academy, and more).
educationBody2: Community outings extend the classroom: college & trade visits, business tours, museums, the Oregon Coast & Columbia River Gorge, and public-transit practice.
educationImageAlt: A wall of inspirational posters inside the home

orientation.label: Week 1
orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.body: Rapport building, resume development, obtaining ID, bus-pass distribution, and a review of program rules & the handbook.

orientation.label: Week 2
orientation.title: Independence
orientation.body: Youth may go out independently as long as they return by curfew, with public-transportation support as needed.

eligibilityBody: Accepted individually after evaluation. Not appropriate for youth needing acute psychiatric care/hospitalization or who are not yet ready for ILP basics.
referralsBody: Referrals must include: reformation plan, OYA Risk-Need Assessment (RNA), current & previous treatment recommendations, parole/probation conditions, juvenile court orders, and social & family histories.
ctaTitle: Have a youth who needs a placement?
ctaLead: Our team is ready to help with referrals and questions.
